key_insight: A machine learning architecture learns holographic quantum circuit syntax and parameters to extrapolate to longer or more expressive circuits.
engineering_relevance: Reusing measured and reset qubits supports sampling large quantum states with fixed qubit resources, while adding qubits exponentially increases the effective bond dimension.
method: Encode states using reusable physical qubits coupled to persistent ancilla qubits.
Learn gate, measurement, and reset sequences alongside rotation parameters from circuit datasets.
Extrapolate learned syntax and parameters to larger circuit instances.
evidence_signal: The methodology is demonstrated on an analytically solvable dataset based on a vector-valued generalization of the W-state; the abstract reports no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the solvable dataset and practical performance under hardware noise remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
